summary.headline: RateGain Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR735.4 crore (+152.6% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA margin 22.7%; FY27 guidance maintained at upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was INR735.4 crore, down about INR40 crore sequentially from Q1 due to a non-recurring FIFA benefit of about USD2.5 million and seasonally softer destination marketing. Organic growth for the combined entity was 14% YoY in Q2 and 15.7% in H1, above the 12-15% FY27 range. Reported EBITDA was INR153 crore (20.5% margin); adjusted EBITDA, after adding back INR16.1 crore of Sojern deferred consideration, was INR169.1 crore (22.7%). Corporate MarTech declined about 14% organically in H1 and is the main drag; management guides it to flat in H2.

financial_highlights.change: +152.6% YoY; down about INR40 crore QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Cash INR239 crore; debt INR733 crore; net debt INR494 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs INR7 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: MarTech (over 80% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew 300% YoY in Q2, mainly from Sojern consolidation. Properties (44.7% of MarTech revenue) and destinations (39.7%) each grew more than 20% organically in H1. Corporate (15.6%) declined about 14% organically in H1, roughly 20% on a constant-currency basis per management.

segments.name: DaaS
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY in Q2 and 14% in H1, versus 22-23% in Q1 on a favorable base. FY27 guidance is double-digit growth in rupee terms.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Broadly flat YoY in Q2. FY27 guided to single-digit growth; management sees potential for double-digit growth in FY28 as Smart Distribution scales.

segments.name: APMEA (within MarTech)
segments.commentary: Record quarter with new sales of about USD2 million, more than 3x a year earlier. More than 50 properties signed on the direct stack in Q2. Middle East revenue about USD500,000 a month in Q2 versus USD970,000 before the disruption.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue maintained at upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore range; implies sequential growth in Q3 and Q4.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided at 22.5%-23.5%, unchanged from last quarter; H1 adjusted margin was 23.7%.
Organic growth guidance of 12-15% for FY27 maintained; medium-term aspiration is 15% constant-currency organic growth.
Corporate MarTech expected to be broadly flat in H2 FY27 and return to growth in FY28 if strategies work.
DMO/destinations business expected to recover sequentially in Q3.
Net debt-free by FY28 maintained; at current pace, net debt positive by end of FY28 per CFO wording.
DaaS double-digit rupee growth for FY27; distribution single-digit for FY27, with double-digit possible in FY28.
capex_capacity: Repaid USD53.75 million of Sojern acquisition debt, about 43% of the original loan, as of the 5 November payment.
Refinanced USD40 million of debt at SOFR plus 165 basis points.
APMEA sales team expanded from about 15 people to about 100.
Smart Distribution live with bookings flowing; more than 800 directly contracted properties connected.
Cloudbeds property ramp-up planned for October; Duetto commercial ramp-up pending advanced partner testing.
Agentic ARI and RateIQ recently launched; expected to contribute to revenue in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Q2 deal wins were strong, mostly in MarTech property (hotels); pipeline is balanced across DaaS, distribution and MarTech, with MarTech the largest share.
Customer additions were cited as 748 in Q2 and 380 in Q3 by an analyst; management attributed additions to hotels/properties.
Corporate wins included a European financial services division, a leading cruise line, a large experiences booking platform and a large vacation rental marketplace; cruise lines are a new vertical.
AirGain airline wins: Philippine Airlines (July), Vietjet Qazaqstan (August), Vietnam Airlines (October).
Google/AI search: management says no impact seen on property marketing budgets (outcome-based model); no inventory-cost increase observed yet.
Management said Europe cross-sell is moving slower than expected, with full traction expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments and industries drove Q2 deal wins, and is the pipeline-to-win conversion sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Most new wins came from MarTech property; pipeline is balanced across DaaS, distribution and MarTech. Management credits APMEA cross-sell and a global key accounts team covering top 10 accounts; one-off large deals were not specifically quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Path to 15% constant-currency organic growth, given Q2 was about 9-10% after adding back Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said arresting the corporate decline could add 200-300 bps. Properties and destinations (over 20% growth) can accelerate further, and integrated booking-engine offerings should reduce churn among low-performing hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be considered, and will the team build-out pressure them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is comfortable above 20% and will reinvest in commercial teams and sales/marketing; AI is reducing build costs. Margin expansion is attributed to cost synergies from consolidating platforms and shared HR and finance services, not currency.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 guidance dependent on DMO recovery, or on other visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects DMO to recover in Q3 (like-for-like Q2 DMO grew over 20% YoY). Corporate moving from about 20% CC decline in H1 to flat in H2 is the main basis for confidence in the upper end of guidance.

qa_highlights.question: DaaS and distribution growth outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: DaaS double-digit rupee growth for FY27; distribution single-digit for FY27, with Smart Distribution expected to create a hockey-stick effect over a couple of quarters and potential double-digit growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is Google AI search shift affecting marketing budgets or ad inventory costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact seen so far. Property budgets are outcome-based and channel-agnostic; corporate decline was attributed to internal focus, not Google. Management is watching AI agent direct bookings as a longer-term risk.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI create scraping-based competition for DaaS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. Defences include anti-blocking technology, formal data partnerships with subscribers, and selective data purchases.

risks_watch: Corporate MarTech decline (about 14% organic in H1, roughly 20% CC) must reverse to flat in H2 to support upper-end revenue guidance.
Middle East revenue still about USD500,000 a month versus USD970,000 pre-disruption; uncertainty persists.
Property churn among low-performing ('bronze' and 'orange') hotels on a pay-for-performance model.
Q3 and Q4 must grow sequentially; H2 growth depends on DMO seasonal recovery and corporate stabilisation.
Airline margin pressure from high fuel costs may affect DaaS air demand; management says volumes have held up.
Europe cross-sell is slower than expected.
Amortization and finance costs are rising, which weigh on PAT; reported PAT margin is 10%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core MarTech and APMEA trajectory and on maintaining guidance, but candid that corporate is a clear problem. Management was more defensive on the corporate decline, attributing it to internal focus rather than external factors. The new CFO's first call was measured and focused on cash and debt reduction.
key_quotes: Organic growth for the combined business was 15.7% in the first half, and if you recall, when we spoke in May, we guided to 12%-15% organic growth for FY27, and the first half is above that range.
We are not seeing any impact.
software is cheap now, and innovation is commoditized.
We expect corporate to be broadly flat in the second half after the decline in the first and to build from there.

Cloudbeds property ramp-up planned for October
Duetto commercial ramp-up pending advanced partner testing

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore and organic growth 12-15% maintained, with H1 organic growth at 15.7%; backing is partial (Q2 deal wins, Smart Distribution live, APMEA sales expansion, Cloudbeds/Duetto ramps) but no capacity or contract figures tied to the guidance, and the reported +152.6% YoY is inflated by the Sojern acquisition consolidation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided at 22.5%-23.5% with H1 at 23.7%, and management says margin gains come from platform consolidation and shared HR/finance cost synergies.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants or capacity figures; the adds are Smart Distribution (live, 800+ properties), Cloudbeds ramp planned for October and a pending Duetto ramp, which are platform capacity rather than capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue held at upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore and organic growth of 12-15% kept, with H1 organic at 15.7% and Q2 deal wins mostly in MarTech property, which requires sequential growth in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given; the focus was on debt repayment (USD53.75m repaid) and refinancing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only held guidance at the upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore and 12-15% organic growth, and H2 needs corporate MarTech to stabilise, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Corporate MarTech is down about 14% organically in H1 (about 20% CC) and must turn flat in H2, while Middle East revenue is about USD500k a month versus USD970k pre-disruption.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic ARI and RateIQ were recently launched and are expected to contribute to revenue in coming quarters, with Duetto and Cloudbeds ramps also pending.

rows.label: Net debt-free by FY28
rows.why: Cash INR239 crore against debt INR733 crore (net debt INR494 crore) and H1 FCF of INR282 crore at 87% EBITDA conversion; management keeps the target, though the CFO said net debt could turn positive by end-FY28 at current pace.

rows.label: APMEA record quarter and Europe cross-sell
rows.why: APMEA new sales of about USD2m in Q2 (over 3x a year earlier) with 50+ properties signed, though Europe cross-sell is slower than expected with full traction pushed to next year.

rows.label: DaaS double-digit and distribution growth
rows.why: DaaS guided to double-digit rupee growth in FY27 (Q2 only +7%, H1 +14%), and distribution to single-digit FY27 growth with potential double-digit in FY28 as Smart Distribution scales.

tone.note: Management was confident on MarTech property, APMEA and holding guidance but defensive on the roughly 14% H1 corporate decline, which it attributed to internal focus; analysts pushed on the path to 15% CC organic growth, the corporate turnaround, and the Middle East and AI-search risks.
